options.summary: Strict Linear Pipeline – A single-threaded, strictly sequential stage pipeline (Intake → Generate → Validate → Review → Patch → Judge → Freeze) where each stage must fully complete and pass its closure gate before the next begins. The orchestrator owns a flat state machine with one active stage at a time. Workspace is a single versioned directory tree with stage-scoped write permissions. Context packs are compiled once per stage transition. Repair loops are bounded intra-stage cycles (patch-revalidate) with a global retry budget.

components.name: Intake Gate
responsibilities: Validate plan_package_final.json against input schema
Validate repo_context.json and workspace_context.json schemas
Initialize run_manifest, event_log, and workspace_index
Emit stage_handoff artifact for Intake→Generate boundary
Reject malformed or incomplete inputs with structured error artifacts

components.name: Work Plan Compiler
responsibilities: Decompose plan_package_final.json R#/AT# entries into ordered implementation tasks
Produce work_plan.json with task dependency graph, acceptance criteria trace, and bounded patchset slots
Map each task to AT# acceptance test IDs for downstream traceability
Enforce CNS5 by verifying no semantic deviation from plan entities

components.name: Code Generator (Writer Role)
responsibilities: Consume context pack compiled by orchestrator for current task
Produce diff-only patchset JSON artifacts per work_plan task
Emit structured code change artifacts with deterministic apply order
Obey tool permission matrix (filesystem read/write scoped to non-forbidden paths)
Output JSON-only artifacts matching per-stage schema (CNS2)

components.name: Validator Engine
responsibilities: Execute build/test/lint/typecheck validators via repo_context.json entrypoints
Produce test_results.json and quality_reports.json with AT# trace mappings
Detect secrets in artifacts and workspace (CNS9)
Enforce forbidden-path and operation-cap rules on patchsets (CNS7)
Emit structured pass/fail results consumed by orchestrator for gate decisions

components.name: Reviewer Pod (Reviewer Role)
responsibilities: Consume patchsets and validation results as read-only context
Produce review_findings.json with RFC 6901 evidence pointers into versioned artifacts
Flag potential scope expansion, risk, or quality issues
Never emit writing or patch artifacts (CNS12 findings-only constraint)
Routed to different vendor/model than writer (multi-vendor separation)

components.name: Patch Repair Agent (Patcher Role)
responsibilities: Consume review findings and validation failures
Produce RFC 6902 JSON Patch arrays for JSON artifact repairs
Produce replacement diff-only patchset artifacts for code repairs
Operate within orchestrator-enforced iteration/op caps
Select smallest passing repair per orchestrator deterministic rules

components.name: Judge Pod (Judge Role)
responsibilities: Independently evaluate patchsets, test results, review findings, and quality reports
Produce trace_report.json confirming evidence pointer completeness
Emit freeze/no-freeze recommendation with structured rationale
Routed to different vendor/model than writer and reviewer
Evaluate risk closure against K# risk entries from plan

components.name: Orchestrator Core
responsibilities: Own the linear state machine: enforce stage ordering and transitions
Compile deterministic context packs per stage from workspace_index
Enforce tool permission matrix per stage/role
Enforce retry budgets, iteration limits, and backoff for flaky failures
Produce stage_handoff artifacts at every checkpoint boundary
Apply deterministic selection logic for smallest passing repair
Trigger HITL escalation or ChangeRequest when thresholds exceeded
Manage secrets redaction/blocking guardrails
Emit final Implementation Freeze Bundle when all gates pass

components.name: Workspace Manager
responsibilities: Maintain versioned workspace directory with canonical vs non-canonical separation
Maintain workspace_index.json with types, versions, provenance for all items
Enforce stage-scoped read/write permissions
Support checkpoint/restore for pause/resume via stage_handoff artifacts
Enforce retention/compaction policies for non-canonical content

components.name: Freeze Assembler
responsibilities: Collect all required freeze bundle artifacts per CNS10

Validate completeness: run_manifest, event_log, work_plan, patchsets, repo_snapshot, test_results, quality_reports, trace_report, review_findings, release_bundle, decision_record, workspace_index, context_packs, stage_handoffs
Produce release_bundle.json and decision_record.json
Run final integrity and reproducibility validators before freeze

interfaces.contract: Orchestrator sends plan_package_final.json, repo_context.json, workspace_context.json; Intake Gate returns validated intake_result.json or structured rejection error.
Intake Gate emits stage_handoff (intake→generate) plus validated input artifacts; Work Plan Compiler reads plan entities and emits work_plan.json.
Orchestrator provides bounded context_pack (workspace artifacts + work_plan task slice + repo state); Writer returns patchset JSON artifacts with diff-embedded changes.
Patchsets applied to repo state by orchestrator; Validator Engine invoked with repo_context.json entrypoints; returns test_results.json + quality_reports.json.
Orchestrator provides read-only context_pack (patchsets + validation results + work_plan); Reviewer returns review_findings.json with RFC 6901 evidence pointers.
Review findings and validation failures provided as context; Patcher returns RFC 6902 patches (JSON) or replacement patchsets (code) within op caps.
Orchestrator provides full context_pack (all artifacts from generate through review/patch); Judge returns freeze_recommendation.json with trace_report.json.
Orchestrator issues versioned read/write/checkpoint/restore commands; Workspace Manager returns workspace_index.json and artifact content. All mutations logged to event_log.
Judge freeze recommendation triggers Freeze Assembler; assembler collects all CNS10-required artifacts and runs final validators; returns freeze_bundle_manifest or failure.
Orchestrator routes validation/review failures to Patcher with bounded iteration budget; Patcher returns candidate repairs; orchestrator selects smallest passing via deterministic rules.

pros: Simplest mental model: one stage active at a time reduces concurrency bugs and makes audit trail trivially sequential
Deterministic ordering makes reproducibility straightforward – replay is a simple linear re-execution
Checkpoint/resume is easy: each stage_handoff is a clean cut point with no in-flight parallel work
Context pack compilation is simpler since only one stage's artifacts need assembly at a time
Easier to reason about tool permissions – each stage has exactly one active permission set
cons: Slowest wall-clock time: no parallelism across independent tasks in the work plan
A single failing task blocks the entire pipeline even if other tasks are independent
Context packs may grow large as all prior stage outputs accumulate linearly
Does not exploit natural parallelism in multi-file or multi-module implementations
Retry/repair cycles for one task delay all subsequent tasks

risks: Long-horizon implementations may exceed token/time budgets due to strictly sequential execution with no parallel task overlap
Large repositories with many independent modules will suffer unnecessary latency from serialized processing
Context pack sizes may exceed model context window limits as the linear pipeline accumulates artifacts without natural partitioning
Flaky test retries in the validate stage can cascade into budget exhaustion since there is no parallel fallback path
Single-threaded repair loops may hit iteration caps before resolving complex multi-file issues that would benefit from decomposition

options.summary: Task-Parallel Fan-Out/Fan-In Pipeline – The work plan is decomposed into independent task groups that can execute Generate→Validate→Review→Patch in parallel lanes, with a deterministic Integration stage that merges patchsets, revalidates, and then proceeds to a single Judge→Freeze sequence. The orchestrator manages a DAG-based state machine with per-lane checkpoints and a merge gate. Workspace uses namespaced partitions per task lane plus a shared canonical partition for merged results.

components.name: Intake & Planning Gate
responsibilities: Validate plan_package_final.json, repo_context.json, workspace_context.json against schemas
Initialize run_manifest, event_log, workspace_index
Decompose plan into work_plan.json with task dependency DAG and parallelism annotations
Identify independent task groups eligible for parallel execution
Emit stage_handoff for Intake→ParallelGenerate boundary

components.name: Task Lane Orchestrator
responsibilities: Spawn parallel execution lanes per independent task group from work_plan DAG
Manage per-lane state machines (Generate→Validate→Review→Patch) independently
Compile per-lane context packs scoped to lane's task slice and relevant repo subset
Enforce per-lane retry budgets and iteration limits
Emit per-lane stage_handoff artifacts at lane checkpoints
Enforce tool permissions scoped to lane's file paths

components.name: Writer Pool (Writer Role, multi-lane)
responsibilities: Each writer instance consumes lane-scoped context pack
Produce diff-only patchset JSON artifacts scoped to lane's file set
Enforce forbidden-path rules within lane scope
Output JSON-only artifacts matching per-stage schema

components.name: Per-Lane Validator
responsibilities: Apply lane patchset to repo state and run scoped validators
Produce per-lane test_results.json and quality_reports.json
Map test results to AT# IDs for traceability
Detect secrets in lane artifacts

components.name: Per-Lane Reviewer (Reviewer Role)
responsibilities: Review lane patchsets and validation results (read-only)
Produce per-lane review_findings.json with RFC 6901 evidence pointers
Flag scope expansion or cross-lane dependency issues
Findings-only: no writing or patch artifacts

components.name: Per-Lane Patcher (Patcher Role)
responsibilities: Consume per-lane review findings and validation failures
Produce repair patches (RFC 6902 for JSON, replacement patchsets for code)
Operate within per-lane iteration/op caps

components.name: Integration Merge Gate
responsibilities: Collect all per-lane patchsets after lane completion
Apply combined patchsets in deterministic order to base repo state
Detect and flag merge conflicts between lanes
Run full-repo validators (build/test/lint/typecheck) on merged state
Produce integrated repo_snapshot.json, test_results.json, quality_reports.json
Escalate unresolvable conflicts via ChangeRequest or HITL

components.name: Judge Pod (Judge Role)
responsibilities: Evaluate integrated results: merged patchsets, full test results, review findings, quality reports
Produce trace_report.json confirming evidence completeness across all lanes
Emit freeze/no-freeze recommendation with structured rationale
Evaluate risk closure against K# entries
Routed to independent vendor/model from writers and reviewers

components.name: Global Orchestrator
responsibilities: Own the top-level DAG state machine: Intake → Parallel Lanes → Integration → Judge → Freeze
Delegate per-lane orchestration to Task Lane Orchestrator
Enforce global retry/iteration budgets across all lanes
Manage workspace namespacing and canonical/non-canonical separation
Compile integration-stage and judge-stage context packs
Trigger HITL/ChangeRequest escalation at global level
Produce stage_handoff artifacts at top-level boundaries
Enforce secrets redaction/blocking across all lanes

components.name: Workspace Manager (Partitioned)
responsibilities: Maintain per-lane workspace partitions with scoped write access
Maintain shared canonical partition for integrated/merged results
Maintain global workspace_index.json covering all partitions
Support per-lane and global checkpoint/restore
Enforce retention/compaction per partition

components.name: Freeze Assembler
responsibilities: Collect all CNS10-required artifacts from integrated results and per-lane outputs
Validate completeness of freeze bundle
Produce release_bundle.json and decision_record.json
Run final integrity, reproducibility, and workspace integrity validators

interfaces.contract: Global orchestrator provides input artifacts; Intake Gate returns validated inputs, work_plan.json with DAG and parallelism annotations, and stage_handoff.
Global orchestrator dispatches independent task groups to Task Lane Orchestrator with lane IDs, task slices, and per-lane budgets; receives per-lane completion signals and stage_handoffs.
Task Lane Orchestrator provides lane-scoped context_pack; Writer returns patchset JSON artifacts scoped to lane file set.
Lane patchsets applied to repo; Per-Lane Validator returns lane test_results.json + quality_reports.json.
Lane context_pack (patchsets + validation) provided read-only; Reviewer returns lane review_findings.json.
Lane failures/findings provided; Patcher returns lane repair patches within lane op caps.

All completed lane patchsets provided with deterministic merge order; Integration Merge Gate returns merged repo_snapshot.json, integrated test_results.json, quality_reports.json, or conflict escalation.
Full integrated context_pack provided; Judge returns freeze_recommendation.json + trace_report.json.
Orchestrator issues namespaced read/write/checkpoint commands per lane or global; Workspace Manager returns workspace_index.json updates. All mutations logged.
Judge freeze recommendation triggers Freeze Assembler; returns freeze_bundle_manifest or failure with missing artifact list.
Integration Merge Gate reports merge conflicts or validation failures; Global Orchestrator decides: re-dispatch conflicting lanes, trigger ChangeRequest, or escalate HITL.

pros: Significantly faster wall-clock time for multi-module/multi-file implementations via parallel task lanes
Independent task failures do not block other lanes, improving resilience
Per-lane context packs are naturally smaller and better scoped than full-pipeline packs
Workspace partitioning provides natural isolation and reduces accidental cross-contamination
Scales naturally with the number of independent tasks in the work plan
cons: Substantially more complex orchestrator logic: DAG scheduling, per-lane budgets, merge conflict resolution
Integration Merge Gate is a complex critical path component requiring deterministic conflict detection and resolution
Per-lane checkpoints and global checkpoints create a more complex resume model
Cross-lane dependencies that are not detected at planning time can cause integration failures
Multi-lane workspace partitioning requires more sophisticated access control and indexing
Higher total token/compute cost due to parallel model invocations and potential redundant context

risks: Merge conflicts between parallel lanes may be frequent in tightly-coupled codebases, causing the Integration Merge Gate to become a bottleneck or require frequent escalation
Task dependency analysis at planning time may miss implicit coupling (shared state, import chains), leading to integration failures that require rework
Per-lane budget allocation may be suboptimal: some lanes finish quickly while others exhaust budgets, and rebalancing adds orchestrator complexity
Workspace partition isolation may be violated if tool execution has side effects outside the lane's scoped paths
Deterministic merge ordering is sensitive to lane completion order; ensuring reproducibility requires explicit ordering rules independent of wall-clock timing

options.summary: Incremental Checkpoint-Driven Pipeline with Partial Freeze – A sequential-by-default pipeline that processes work_plan tasks one at a time (or in small batches) through a micro-cycle (Generate→Validate→Review→Patch per task), checkpointing after each task. Supports partial freezes: if budget/time limits are reached, the system can freeze completed tasks as a partial Implementation Freeze Bundle with explicit incomplete-task metadata, enabling deterministic resume from the last checkpoint. Designed for long-horizon execution where full completion in one run is not guaranteed.

components.name: Intake & Work Plan Compiler
responsibilities: Validate inputs (plan_package_final.json, repo_context.json, workspace_context.json)
Initialize or resume run_manifest, event_log, workspace_index from prior checkpoint if resuming
Produce or update work_plan.json with task ordering and completion status
Detect resume scenario and load prior stage_handoff for continuation
Emit stage_handoff for Intake→TaskCycle boundary

components.name: Task Cycle Engine
responsibilities: Execute micro-cycles per task: Generate→Validate→Review→Patch
Checkpoint workspace and emit stage_handoff after each completed task
Track cumulative budget consumption (tokens, time, retries)
Signal orchestrator when budget thresholds are approaching
Support small-batch parallel execution for independent adjacent tasks when enabled

components.name: Writer (Writer Role)
responsibilities: Consume task-scoped context pack for current micro-cycle
Produce diff-only patchset JSON for current task
Enforce forbidden paths and scope constraints
JSON-only output per CNS2

components.name: Task Validator
responsibilities: Apply task patchset and run incremental validators (affected tests, lint on changed files)
Produce incremental test_results.json and quality_reports.json
Map results to AT# IDs
Detect secrets

components.name: Task Reviewer (Reviewer Role)
responsibilities: Review task patchset and incremental validation results (read-only)
Produce task review_findings.json with RFC 6901 evidence pointers
Findings-only constraint enforced

components.name: Task Patcher (Patcher Role)
responsibilities: Consume task-level findings and failures
Produce repair patches within task-scoped op caps
Orchestrator selects smallest passing repair

components.name: Regression Revalidation Gate
responsibilities: After each task micro-cycle, run full-repo validators on cumulative repo state
Detect regressions introduced by latest task's patchset
Produce cumulative test_results.json overlay
Trigger repair cycle or rollback if regression detected

components.name: Judge Pod (Judge Role)
responsibilities: Evaluate cumulative state when all tasks complete or at partial freeze boundary
Produce trace_report.json for completed tasks
Emit freeze or partial-freeze recommendation
Assess risk closure for completed scope
Independent vendor/model routing

components.name: Orchestrator Core (Checkpoint-Oriented)
responsibilities: Own sequential task-by-task state machine with per-task checkpoints
Monitor budget consumption and decide continue vs partial-freeze
Compile task-scoped context packs with sliding window over recent workspace state
Enforce tool permissions, retry budgets, iteration limits per task
Produce stage_handoff at every task boundary enabling deterministic resume
Manage partial freeze logic: mark incomplete tasks, record resume point
Trigger HITL/ChangeRequest when task failures exceed thresholds
Enforce secrets redaction/blocking

components.name: Workspace Manager (Append-Checkpoint Model)
responsibilities: Maintain workspace with append-only checkpoint log per task completion
Maintain workspace_index.json with per-task provenance and completion status
Support deterministic restore to any task checkpoint
Separate canonical (completed task outputs) from non-canonical (in-progress notes)
Enforce compaction policies for non-canonical content at checkpoint boundaries

components.name: Freeze / Partial-Freeze Assembler
responsibilities: Assemble full or partial Implementation Freeze Bundle
For partial freeze: include completion_status in run_manifest indicating completed vs pending tasks
Include all CNS10 artifacts for completed scope; mark pending artifacts as absent with reason
Run integrity/reproducibility validators on completed scope
Produce resume_descriptor artifact enabling deterministic continuation run

interfaces.contract: Orchestrator provides input artifacts or prior stage_handoff for resume; Intake returns validated inputs or resumed state plus work_plan.json with completion status.
Orchestrator dispatches next task (or small batch) to Task Cycle Engine with task-scoped budget; receives task completion signal, updated patchsets, and stage_handoff.
Task Cycle Engine provides task-scoped context_pack; Writer returns patchset JSON for task.
Task patchset applied; Validator returns incremental test_results.json + quality_reports.json.
Task context_pack (patchset + validation) provided read-only; Reviewer returns task review_findings.json.
Task failures/findings provided; Patcher returns task-scoped repair patches.
After each task completion, orchestrator triggers Regression Revalidation with cumulative repo state; gate returns cumulative validation results or regression alert.
At completion or partial-freeze boundary, orchestrator provides cumulative context_pack; Judge returns freeze/partial-freeze recommendation + trace_report.json.
Orchestrator issues checkpoint/restore/append commands per task; Workspace Manager returns updated workspace_index.json. All mutations logged.
Judge recommendation triggers Freeze/Partial-Freeze Assembler; returns full or partial freeze_bundle_manifest with completion_status and resume_descriptor.
Regression gate reports regression; orchestrator decides: repair cycle on current task, rollback task patchset, escalate via ChangeRequest, or HITL.

pros: Naturally handles long-horizon execution: partial freeze enables progress preservation when budgets are exhausted
Per-task checkpointing provides fine-grained resume with minimal rework on restart
Task-scoped context packs stay small and focused, reducing context window pressure
Regression revalidation after each task catches issues early before they compound
Simpler than full parallel fan-out while still making incremental progress
Partial freeze bundles provide value even when full implementation is not achievable in one run
cons: Sequential task execution is slower than parallel approaches for independent tasks
Regression revalidation after every task adds overhead proportional to task count × full validation cost
Partial freeze introduces complexity in downstream consumers that must handle incomplete bundles
Resume logic must perfectly reconstruct prior state from checkpoint, adding implementation complexity
Small-batch parallelism (optional) adds complexity without the full benefit of the fan-out approach
Cumulative repo state may diverge from expectations if early tasks create unexpected dependencies for later tasks

risks: Regression revalidation cost may become prohibitive for large repos with slow test suites, creating pressure to skip or weaken validation
Partial freeze bundles may not be accepted by downstream consumers that expect complete implementations, requiring additional contract negotiation
Resume from checkpoint may encounter environment drift (dependency versions, tool versions) if significant time passes between runs
Task ordering in work_plan may create implicit dependencies that cause later tasks to fail due to assumptions about earlier task outputs
Budget estimation for partial-freeze decisions is inherently uncertain; the orchestrator may freeze too early or too late

options.summary: Layered Council with Dedicated Integration Council – Separates the implementation workflow into two sub-councils: an Implementation Sub-Council that produces per-module patchsets via parallel or sequential task execution, and a dedicated Integration Sub-Council that merges, revalidates, reviews, and judges the combined output. Each sub-council has its own orchestrator loop, workspace partition, and freeze gate, with a top-level Council Coordinator managing the handoff. This mirrors the Planning Council's separation-of-concerns pattern at a higher level of abstraction.

components.name: Council Coordinator
responsibilities: Top-level orchestrator managing handoff between Intake, Implementation Sub-Council, and Integration Sub-Council
Enforce global budgets, HITL triggers, and ChangeRequest escalation
Produce top-level stage_handoff artifacts at sub-council boundaries
Compile cross-council context packs for Integration Sub-Council intake
Own the global run_manifest and event_log

components.name: Intake Gate
responsibilities: Validate plan_package_final.json, repo_context.json, workspace_context.json
Initialize run_manifest, event_log, workspace_index
Produce work_plan.json with module/component decomposition and dependency graph
Emit stage_handoff for Intake→Implementation Sub-Council

components.name: Implementation Sub-Council Orchestrator
responsibilities: Manage internal staged workflow for code generation per module/task
Support parallel or sequential task execution within sub-council scope
Compile task-scoped context packs from sub-council workspace partition
Enforce per-task tool permissions, retry budgets, iteration limits
Checkpoint per task and emit sub-council stage_handoffs
Produce per-module patchsets, test_results, quality_reports, review_findings

components.name: Implementation Writer Pool
responsibilities: Produce diff-only patchsets per module/task
Consume task-scoped context packs
Enforce forbidden paths and JSON-only output

components.name: Implementation Validator Pool
responsibilities: Run per-module validators (build, test, lint scoped to module)
Produce per-module test_results.json and quality_reports.json
Map to AT# IDs
Detect secrets

components.name: Implementation Reviewer Pool
responsibilities: Review per-module patchsets and validation results (findings-only)
Produce per-module review_findings.json with RFC 6901 evidence pointers
Different vendor/model from writers

components.name: Implementation Patcher Pool
responsibilities: Repair per-module failures via RFC 6902 patches or replacement patchsets
Operate within per-module op caps

components.name: Integration Sub-Council Orchestrator
responsibilities: Manage internal staged workflow: Merge→FullValidate→IntegrationReview→IntegrationPatch→Judge
Consume all per-module outputs from Implementation Sub-Council
Compile integration-scoped context packs
Enforce integration-specific tool permissions and budgets
Checkpoint at each integration stage

components.name: Merge Engine
responsibilities: Apply all per-module patchsets in deterministic order to base repo
Detect merge conflicts and file-level collisions
Produce merged repo_snapshot.json
Escalate unresolvable conflicts to Council Coordinator

components.name: Integration Validator
responsibilities: Run full-repo validators on merged state
Produce integrated test_results.json and quality_reports.json
Verify no regressions from per-module to integrated state

components.name: Integration Reviewer (Reviewer Role)
responsibilities: Review integrated patchsets and full validation results (findings-only)
Focus on cross-module interactions, integration issues, and holistic quality
Produce integration review_findings.json
Different vendor/model from implementation reviewers and writers

components.name: Integration Patcher
responsibilities: Repair integration-level failures
Produce integration repair patches within integration op caps

components.name: Judge Pod (Judge Role)
responsibilities: Evaluate fully integrated and validated results
Produce trace_report.json covering all modules and integration
Emit freeze/no-freeze recommendation
Evaluate risk closure against all K# entries
Independent vendor/model from all writers, reviewers, patchers

components.name: Workspace Manager (Dual-Partition)
responsibilities: Maintain Implementation Sub-Council workspace partition (per-module namespaces)
Maintain Integration Sub-Council workspace partition (merged/integrated artifacts)
Maintain unified workspace_index.json spanning both partitions
Support checkpoint/restore per sub-council
Enforce canonical vs non-canonical separation in both partitions

components.name: Freeze Assembler
responsibilities: Collect all CNS10-required artifacts from both sub-councils
Validate freeze bundle completeness
Produce release_bundle.json and decision_record.json
Run final integrity, reproducibility, and workspace integrity validators

interfaces.contract: Coordinator provides input artifacts; Intake returns validated inputs, work_plan.json, and stage_handoff.
Coordinator dispatches work_plan task groups to Implementation Sub-Council with budgets; receives sub-council completion signal with all per-module artifacts and stage_handoff.
Sub-council orchestrator provides task-scoped context_pack; Writer returns patchset JSON.
Patchsets applied; Validator returns per-module test_results.json + quality_reports.json.
Per-module context provided read-only; Reviewer returns per-module review_findings.json.
Per-module failures provided; Patcher returns repair patches within op caps.
Coordinator provides all Implementation Sub-Council outputs to Integration Sub-Council with integration budget; receives integration completion signal and stage_handoff.
Integration orchestrator provides per-module patchsets with merge order; Merge Engine returns merged repo_snapshot.json or conflict report.
Merged repo state provided; Integration Validator returns full-repo test_results.json + quality_reports.json.
Integrated context provided read-only; Integration Reviewer returns integration review_findings.json.
Integration failures provided; Integration Patcher returns integration repair patches.
Coordinator provides full integrated context_pack; Judge returns freeze_recommendation.json + trace_report.json.
Coordinator issues workspace commands for both partitions; Workspace Manager returns unified workspace_index.json.
Judge freeze recommendation triggers Freeze Assembler; returns freeze_bundle_manifest or failure.

pros: Strongest separation of concerns: implementation and integration are independently governed sub-councils with their own budgets, validators, and checkpoints
Integration Sub-Council provides dedicated review of cross-module interactions by specialized reviewers, catching issues that per-module review misses
Mirrors CouncilOS council-of-councils pattern, making it conceptually consistent with the broader system
Each sub-council can evolve independently (e.g., swap Implementation Sub-Council's internal strategy without affecting Integration Sub-Council)
Dual-partition workspace provides strong isolation between implementation and integration artifacts
Integration reviewers see the holistic picture, providing a second layer of quality assurance beyond per-module review
cons: Most complex architecture: two orchestrator loops plus a coordinator, with three levels of checkpoint/resume logic
Highest overhead in terms of total model invocations (implementation review + integration review + judge)
Handoff between sub-councils is a complex interface requiring comprehensive artifact transfer
Workspace duplication across partitions increases storage requirements
Debugging and auditing spans three orchestration levels, making trace analysis more complex
Over-engineered for small implementations where a single-council approach would suffice

risks: Three-level orchestration (coordinator + two sub-council orchestrators) creates significant implementation complexity and potential for subtle state synchronization bugs
Integration Sub-Council may duplicate significant validation work already done per-module, inflating cost without proportional quality improvement
Handoff contract between sub-councils may become a bottleneck if artifact volume is large or schemas evolve independently
The coordinator's global budget allocation between sub-councils is a non-trivial optimization problem; misallocation wastes resources
Resume across sub-council boundaries requires coordinating checkpoint state at three levels, increasing the risk of inconsistent resume states
